acceptance: A read-only audit-report.md that a phase plants in the workspace before the first audit dispatch never reaches deferDecision, the dossier or the retro floor; the host removes it before audit round 0, or the audit deliverable check rejects a report the auditor of this round did not write (red first: plant the file, run an audit whose runner writes nothing, and show phasecontract.ReadFailureBlock(ws, "audit") feeds the defer)

The core test fixtures that pre-write audit-report.md for a fake auditor write it from the fake audit runner instead, so the round-0 clear does not break them (13 tests in internal/core fail with a plain round-0 remove)
Audit rounds 1 and later keep today's archive behaviour byte for byte
fix: At audit round 0, remove audit-report.md and acs-verdict.json from the workspace before the dispatch (WARN when one was present), the same fresh-input rule as clearRetroDecisionInput, and move the fixtures that plant an audit report into their fake audit runners.
summary: deferDecision reads the audit failure block first (phasecontract.ReadFailureBlock(ws, "audit"), reintent_decision.go). retireSupersededAuditArtifacts returns early when round < 1 (audit_round_artifacts.go:33), so an audit-report.md that the builder plants before the first audit is not retired by the host. A plain round-0 remove is correct for production but breaks 13 core tests whose fixtures pre-write the report for a fake auditor. It was not verified end to end whether the auditor's deliverable check rejects a stale report that it could not overwrite. ADR-0072 names this as a limit of D4.
title: An audit-report.md planted before the first audit is a defer input the host never cleared
